_comment: Import policy for scripts/check-import-graph.py. Encodes plan section 3.2's allowed-dependency matrix. known_cycles are MEASURED on the current tree, not invented: the plan (P0.4) says to record existing cycles rather than fix them during a structural step, and to block only NEW ones.
_known_cycles_note:
The first cycle was `controlled_emulation <-> emulation_plan <-> investigation <-> static_analysis`. IT NO LONGER EXISTS and the entry was retired in round 78: P2-V.0 moved the thread-start predicate group into `facts/thread_start.py`, which removed the `static_analysis -> investigation` leg - the whole reason that leg existed was one predicate borrowed from the investigation layer. The gate reported the cycle count falling from 2 to 1 and this entry becoming stale; retiring it is the deliberate follow-through, not a loosening.

(2) BOTH cycles are now retired and the allowlist is EMPTY, which is the state the plan wants: the module graph has no cycles at all.

`service <-> tool_execution` was retired by P2-T.0. MEASURED: `tool_execution.py` had NO module-level package imports at all - the reverse leg was two FUNCTION-LEVEL `from threat_report_agent.service import AnalysisService` statements inside `StaticToolActivities.expire_model_payloads` and `.seal_daily_audit`, which the gate sees because it walks every AST node. Plan 7.5 requires the cycle to be unwound before the tool layer moves into `tools/`, and its failure clause forbids carrying it into the new package. A port could not do it: the composition root that would inject the port (`run_static_worker`) lived in the same module, so injecting the service from there would still be a `tools -> service` dependency. P2-T.0 therefore SEPARATED the two planes: the retention and audit-seal activities, their two workflows, their two schedules and the worker composition root moved into `src/threat_report_agent/control_activities.py`, leaving `control_activities -> service -> tool_execution` and `control_activities -> tool_execution`, with no path back from the tool layer. The gate reported the count falling from 1 to 0.

An allowlist entry that permits a cycle which no longer exists cannot notice that cycle returning, so it is removed rather than kept as documentation. `tests/test_control_plane_contract.py` pins the replacement: the tool module must have no service reference at any nesting depth, the registered activity names per worker role must be unchanged, and both workflows must dispatch the same activity names.
_forbidden_edges_note: Direction rules from plan section 3.2: facts/static/emulation/tools/intake must not import the service or the report layer, and facts/ must not depend on emulation/. The flat-module names are listed alongside the future package names because the migration leaves shims that keep both names alive; enforcing only the package names would let a reverse edge survive under the old name. The `service -> forbidden` direction is NOT encoded because service.py legitimately orchestrates every layer: plan section 3.2 places task/ above all of them. ACCEPTED EDGE (user decision, round 96): `facts -> investigation` is DELIBERATELY PERMITTED. P2-V.8 moved the dependency-free predicate module `semantic_predicates` into `investigation/`, so `facts/dataflow.py` and `facts/thread_start.py` import it from there. The direction is recorded as a DECISION rather than an oversight: if `facts` must later sit strictly at the bottom, the correct move is to push that pure predicate down into `facts/` FIRST and only then declare the edge forbidden - both halves together, never one alone. See `docs/plan-conflict-resolutions-20260922.md`, decision (a). ALLOWED edges that the matrix does not list are recorded in `recorded_allowed_edges` (see its note): an unlisted edge needs a decision, not a gate citation.
_known_violations_note: MEASURED pre-existing violation of the rule above: persist_how imports reporting, and plan section 3.2's allow-list for the layer that owns persist_how does not include the report layer ('未列出的边默认禁止'). It is RECORDED rather than fixed, because plan P0.4 forbids rewriting business logic during a structural step and P1.4 forbids smuggling a behaviour change into one. --strict therefore fails only on violations NOT in this list, so a NEW reverse edge is still blocked. Unwinding this one belongs with the P1.2 ports.
_p13_note: The three keys below are what scripts/check-structure-diff.py --structure compares against. Each is MEASURED on the current tree (never invented) and registered in the same spirit as known_violations: P1.3's success criterion is that a PURE MOVE PASSES, so a pre-existing instance must be recorded rather than fixed inside a structural step, while any NEW instance fails --strict. Every entry states what it is, so an allowlist entry cannot be mistaken for an approval.
_moved_paths_public_path_unchanged_note: The last entry is a MODULE -> PACKAGE move: `threat_report_agent.investigation` was a module and is now the package whose implementation is `investigation/investigation.py`. Its PUBLIC dotted path did not change, so `public_path_unchanged: true` tells scripts/check-structure-diff.py's old-path rule to SKIP it (production importers of `threat_report_agent.investigation` are correct, not legacy - there is nothing to migrate), while scripts/check-import-graph.py still uses the entry to normalise `investigation.investigation` back to `investigation`, so the recorded 4-module cycle keeps matching instead of reporting as NEW.
_moved_paths_note: The canonical rename map, and the SINGLE SOURCE for it: scripts/check-import-graph.py normalises module names through it and scripts/check-structure-diff.py derives its old-path rule from it. WHY IT EXISTS (MEASURED in round 74): moving `static_analysis.py` into `static/` made the recorded cycle `controlled_emulation <-> emulation_plan <-> investigation <-> static_analysis` report as NEW, because the graph now spells the member `static.static_analysis` while the allowlist spells it `static_analysis`. The cycle did not change; only one member's name did. Normalising through this map is the fix, and it means the rest of P2 and all of P4 need no policy edit per move. Before this map existed the same information was duplicated in a constant inside check-structure-diff.py, which had to be hand-edited on every move. Round 79 added the four model-layer modules (prompts, agent_runtime, agents, model_gateway) after P2-M moved them; like the static and emulation entries their registered old-path importer count is ZERO because production moved first.

known_private_reach.note: MEASURED: AnalysisService reads its OWN private attribute by string name, defensively (the attribute may not exist, hence the getattr default). It is recorded rather than fixed because the fix is to declare the attribute on the class, which is a behaviour-visible edit and belongs to P3's split of AnalysisService. Unlike the plan's named example it does NOT reach across classes.

_legacy_path_imports_note: MEASURED importers of a path that has already moved. The migration left `sys.modules` shims at the old paths, so these imports still work - which is exactly why they must be enumerated: an unregistered old-path import is how a moved implementation keeps a second access path alive, and plan 7.1 step 5 says production callers move to the new path FIRST. This ONE is the remaining P4.1 work item; any importer NOT listed here fails --strict. (CORRECTED in round 96: this sentence said FOUR while the list held one entry. The count was measured against the data - `len(legacy_path_imports) == 1` - and the prose was the stale part, so it was fixed rather than the entry being padded out.) TWO ENTRIES WERE REMOVED IN ROUND 74, not re-registered: `threat_report_agent.static_analysis` was the last importer of `dataflow` and `decode_primitives` by their old paths, and when it moved into `static/` its imports were migrated to `facts.dataflow` / `facts.decode_primitives` in the same step - so the ledger shrank from 6 to 4 because the code changed, and the gate reported the two entries as stale before they were deleted.
_known_duplicate_note: EMPTY as of P2-V.1. The ONE recorded duplication was `_function_call_names`, byte-identical in `investigation_protocol.py` and `report/reporting.py` (name-inclusive body hash b2bbbaac53b5835a, body-only hash 0c5ca4fb1ca89f71). It was resolved by keeping the canonical implementation in `investigation_protocol.py` - chosen because `investigation_protocol -> reporting` is a FORBIDDEN edge while `reporting -> investigation_protocol` already existed, so this direction added no edge - renaming it to the PUBLIC `function_call_names` (it is imported across modules now, so a private cross-module reach would be the wrong shape), and deleting the copy. Nothing was reimplemented: the surviving body is byte-identical to both HEAD copies. Note for future readers: `body_sha256` in these records is NAME-INCLUSIVE, so renaming a recorded function changes its hash even when its body does not; compare bodies with the name normalised out.
_recorded_allowed_edges_note: Edges that section 3.2's matrix does not list but that a recorded DECISION accepts. The gate does NOT read this key today: `forbidden_edges` is a deny-list and the matrix is not machine-encoded, so an unlisted edge cannot be machine-checked at all - that blind spot is stated here rather than hidden. The decision and its measurements are in `docs/plan-conflict-resolutions-20260922.md` decision (d). MEASURED round 106: `model.model_gateway -> contracts` exists because `DynamicPlanAction` moved into the pure contract layer so that (a) `investigation/` may import it (matrix line 132) and (b) the model port can expose it WITHOUT importing httpx (the gateway imports httpx; `ports.py` documents itself as free of transport/SDK imports). Cycle count stayed 0 and no forbidden edge was hit. To machine-check this class of decision, encode the matrix as an allow-list and make check-import-graph.py --strict fail on any unregistered edge. DECISION (d1) ADDED round 145: `emulation -> models` is ACCEPTED and registered for the P3.5 `EmulationCoordinator` (`docs/decision-d1-emulation-imports-models-20260922.md`). MEASURED rationale rather than taste: `models` is omitted from EVERY row of section 3.2's matrix, and 11 modules across four packages already import it (`static/evidence_recovery.py`, `investigation/{coordinator,derivation,persist_how,seed_support}.py`, `task/{task_runner,limitations,analysis_task_orchestration}.py`, `tools/tool_execution.py`, `database.py`, `service.py`), so refusing it to `emulation/` alone would be the matrix's only baseless exception. CONDITIONS: the edge is for the coordinator's row persistence and id generation only (8 names); `service`, `report`, HTTP and DSH stay forbidden for `emulation/`; and the non-persisting emulation modules (`policy.py`, `vb6_runtime_shim.py`, `emulation_plan.py`) keep importing only the standard library plus `facts`/`static`. MEASURED LIMIT, stated so registration is not mistaken for enforcement: `py scripts/check-import-graph.py` reads this key solely to populate its node registry (`registered.update(...)`) and never compares an edge against it, so with 258 runtime edges on the tree and 4 recorded entries the strict gate is green either way. Only 3 of the 11 `-> models` edges are now registered; encoding section 3.2 as an allow-list so that `--strict` fails on ANY unregistered edge remains its own step and is the same fix P3.6-2's design asks for.
_known_modules_note: Every module must be REGISTERED here (or by another policy entry) or `--strict` fails, because the deny-list can only police names it knows: a module created after this policy was written would otherwise be invisible and could import a forbidden layer GREEN (measured in round 134 with `emulation/coordinator.py -> report.reporting`). Generated in round 135 from the gate's own output; a new module must be added in the same commit that creates it.
_known_private_reach_note: WIDENED at P3.5-0 (round 148): the metric used to count only dynamic reaches (`getsource(._x)`, `getattr(obj, "_x")`) and therefore reported a total of 1 while an AST count of `from <other module> import _name` edges inside the package found 41. Static private imports are now counted as their own shape and the pre-existing set is recorded here. The record must match the measurement EXACTLY (the gate's own anti-evasion rule), so a new private import fails `--strict` and removing a recorded one fails until this list is updated deliberately.
